Rashi on Eruvin 55b:13:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה משום בנין - אם יש בנין על פיה, מאי אהניא מערה? בלאו מערה נמי, מבנין משחינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:13:1.english: And let him derive [it] because of the structure - If there is a structure at its entrance, of what benefit is the cave? Even without the cave, we would also measure from the structure.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:13:2.hebrew: להשלים - אם אין הבנין ראוי לדירה, כגון שאין בו ד' על ד' — מהניא ליה מערה לאשלומי:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:13:2.english: To complete - If the structure is not fit for a dwelling, such as where it does not have four by four [cubits], the cave is effective for it to complete [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:14:1.hebrew: צריפין - דירה של הוצין וערבה, ואינו קבע. הלכך, אפילו יש הרבה במקום אחד כשיעור מהלך מאה אמה, אין חשובין עיר להיות כארבע אמות, וכל אחד מודד מפתח ביתו אלפים לכל רוח, אם בא לצאת:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:14:1.english: Huts - A dwelling [made] of palm fronds and willows, and it is not permanent. Therefore, even if there are many [of them] in one place, spanning a walking distance of one hundred cubits, they are not considered a city such that [the entire area] is regarded as four cubits; and each [person] measures two thousand [cubits] in each direction from the entrance of his house, if he wishes to go out.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:15:1.english: And they pitched by the Jordan - It is written regarding the camp of Israel.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:1.hebrew: אין נפנין לא לפניהן - חוץ לענן, שמא ילך הענן והארון שם:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:1.english: They do not relieve themselves, not in front of them - Outside the cloud, lest the cloud and the Ark go there.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:2.hebrew: ולא לצידיהן - חוץ לענן, שאין יודעין אנה יפנה הענן לעבור:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:2.english: Nor to their sides - Outside the cloud, for they do not know which way the cloud will turn to travel.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:3.hebrew: אלא לאחוריהן - חוץ לענן, דודאי לא יחזור הענן לאחוריו. אלמא, המהלך בראש והוצרך לנקביו חוזר לאחוריו שלש פרסאות; וישראל במדבר יושבי אהלים היו שאינן קבועין, ואפילו הכי מהלכין את כל המחנה כארבע אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:16:3.english: Rather, behind them - Outside the cloud, for the cloud certainly will not turn backwards. It follows that one who was walking at the front [of the camp] and needed to relieve himself would walk back behind him three parasangs; and Israel in the wilderness were dwellers of tents that are not permanent, and even so, they [could] walk the entire camp as [if it were] four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:17:1.english: Since it is written: “According to the commandment of the Lord they encamped” - Their encampment is significant [enough] to be considered permanent.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:18:1.hebrew: ג' חצירות של ב' בתים - קבועין של אבן או של עץ, בהכי חשיבי עיר, וקובעת את כולן. וכדתנן לקמן (עירובין דף נט.), ר' שמעון אומר: שלש חצירות של ב' ב' בתים:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:18:1.english: Three courtyards of two houses - [Houses that are] permanent, of stone or of wood. With this [amount], it is considered a town, and [the town] establishes all of them [the huts], as we learned below (Eruvin 59a): Rabbi Shimon says: Three courtyards of two houses each.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:19:1.english: And desert travelers - And their wives are with them.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:19:2.english: Are not their own - Below, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:1:1.hebrew: נותנין קרפף לעיר - כשבא למדוד התחומין, מניח לעיר אויר של שבעים אמה ושיריים, שהוא כעיר, לבד התחום:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:1:1.english: One allocates a karpef to a city - When one comes to measure the [Sabbath] limits, one leaves for the city an open space of seventy cubits and a fraction, which is [considered] like the city [itself], aside from the [Sabbath] limit.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:1:2.hebrew: אלא לב' עיירות - לחברן על ידי קרפף שביניהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:1:2.english: Only for two cities - To join them by means of a karpef that is between them.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:20:1.hebrew: כיושבי קברות - כמתים, לפי שמחוסרין הנאה הן, ולוקין ברוחות, בזרם ובמטר:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:20:1.english: Like those who dwell in graves - Like the dead, since they lack pleasure, and suffer from winds, from downpours, and from rain.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:21:1.english: What is the reason - [Because] their daughters are forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:21:2.hebrew: שאין להן מרחצאות - והולכין במקום רחוק לרחוץ, ונשותיהן נזקקות למנאפין, לפי שהעיר עזובה מאין איש:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:21:2.english: That they do not have bathhouses - And [the men] go to a distant place to bathe, and their wives submit to adulterers, because the town is deserted, with no man [present].

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:21:3.hebrew: בטבילה - שאין להן מקוואות, והולכות הנשים לטבול במקום רחוק, וקוראה לחברתה, ומרגישין השכנים, ויש רשע רודף אחריהן ומתייחד עמהן. ותנן (קידושין דף פ:): לא יתייחד אדם עם שתי נשים:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:21:3.english: Regarding [ritual] immersion - For they do not have ritual baths, and the women go to immerse in a distant place, and [a woman] calls to her companion, and the neighbors notice, and there is a wicked man who pursues them and secludes himself with them. And we learned in a mishna (Kiddushin 80b): A man may not seclude himself with two women.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:22:1.hebrew: נהרא - ראוי לטבילה ולא למרחץ. הרגש טבילה ליכא, דהא סמוך לה; אבל טעמא דמשום מרחצאות איכא:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:22:1.english: A river - [Which is] suitable for immersion, but not for bathing. Awareness of immersion does not apply, for behold, [it] is close to it [the city]; but the reason regarding bathhouses does apply.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:23:1.hebrew: אין תלמיד חכם כו' - לפי שהירק טוב למאכל ונלקח בזול, ויכול לעסוק בתורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:23:1.english: A Torah scholar is not [permitted], etc. - Because vegetables are good for food and purchased cheaply, and [so] he is able to engage in Torah [study].

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:2:1.english: And it was stated: Rav Huna said, etc. - And later in the chapter [the Gemara] explains their dispute.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:3:1.hebrew: אי אשמעינן - בחומת העיר שנפרצה, התם קאמר רב הונא קרפף לזו ולזו לחברן, משום דהוה להו צד היתר מעיקרא, שהיו כבר עיר אחת:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:3:1.english: Had he taught us - In [the case of] the city wall that was breached, [one might have said that only] there did Rav Huna say [to allocate] a karpef to this [section] and to that [section] to join them, because they had an aspect of permissibility from the outset, as they were already one city.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:4:1.hebrew: דדחיקא תשמישתייהו - ב' עיירות ממש, דחיקא תשמישתייהו בחד קרפף. הלכך, קרפף מיחשב לכל חד כעיר גופה. וכיון דצריך לה והוי כעיר, כי מחברי ב' הקרפיפות — כאילו העיירות מחוברות דמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:4:1.english: Because their use is cramped - [In the case of] two actual cities, their use is cramped with [only] one karpef. Therefore, a karpef is considered for each one like the city itself. And since [each city] needs it and it is [treated] like the city, when the two karpefot connect, they are considered as though the cities [themselves] are connected.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:4:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - דעיר אחת היא, ומעיקרא, כי מחברי קודם שנפרצה, הויא כולה מלאה והוי סגיא לה בלאו האי אויר, השתא נמי לא ניתיב האי אוירה לתשמישן — קמ"ל:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:4:2.english: But here - Since it is a single city, and originally, when it was joined together before it was breached, it was entirely full and it was sufficient for it without this open space, [one might say that] now too we should not grant this open space for their use — [therefore,] it teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:5:1.hebrew: וכמה - יהא אויר החלק מן היתר לקשת, דאמרו מודדין לה מן היתר כי ליכא ארבעת אלפים בין ב' ראשיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:5:1.english: And how much - [May] the open space from the bowstring to the bow be, that they said one measures for it from the bowstring when there are not four thousand [cubits] between its two ends?

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:5:2.hebrew: אלפים - אבל יותר מאלפים, כיון דמכי נפק מביתו הולך לו תחום שלם מקמי דלימטי ליתר, לא משחינן ליה מן היתר:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:5:2.english: Two thousand - But [if there is] more than two thousand [cubits], since once he leaves his house he walks a full [Shabbat] limit before he reaches the bowstring, we do not measure for him from the bowstring.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:6:1.hebrew: דאי בעי הדר אתי - למקום היתר, דרך הבתים סביב הקשת, יכול להלך עד שמגיע לאחד מן הראשון, ומשם יכול להלך לראשו האחר, שהרי תחומיהן נבלעין זה בזה. וכיון דבהיתר יכול להלך למקום היתר, תו לא אסר ליה אורך החלק לשוויה כשתי עיירות, ורואין אותה כאילו היא מלאה בתים וחצירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:6:1.english: For if he wants, he can return and come - To the place of the bowstring, by way of the houses around the bow, he can walk until he reaches one of the ends [of the bow], and from there he can walk to its other end, for their [Shabbat] limits are merged into one another. And since he can permissibly walk to the place of the bowstring, the length of the vacant space no longer renders it forbidden so as to make it like two cities, and we view it as though it were filled with houses and courtyards.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:7:1.hebrew: שאין עליהן תקרה - וכל שכן אם מקורות הן מזו לזו בגג, דהוו להו דירה מעלייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:7:1.english: That do not have a roof over them - And all the more so if they are covered from one to the other with a roof, for they [then] constitute a proper dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:1.hebrew: נפש - בנין על הקבר, וסתמא לדירת שומר הקבר עביד. הלכך, אע"ג דלא דייר ביה — בית דירה הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:1.english: A monument [nefesh] - A structure over a grave. And ordinarily it is made for the dwelling of the watchman of the grave; therefore, even though one does not [presently] dwell in it, it is a dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:3.hebrew: ובית הכנסת - סתם ביהכ"נ לאו לדירה עביד. הלכך, אי לית בה דירה לחזן הכנסת — לאו דירה היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:3.english: And a synagogue - An ordinary synagogue is not made for dwelling; therefore, if there is no residence in it for the synagogue attendant, it is not a dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:4.english: And an idolatrous temple - [It] is also not made for dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:6.hebrew: אוצרות - לתבואה ולשמן וליין, לאו לדירה נינהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:6.english: Storehouses - [Storehouses] for grain, and for oil, and for wine; they are not for dwelling.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:7.english: And the watchtowers that are within it - Within the field.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:8.hebrew: והבית שבים - באיי הים, בתוך ע' אמה ושיריים לעיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:8:8.english: And the house that is in the sea - On islands in the sea, within seventy cubits and a remainder from the city.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:9:1.english: A cistern and a ditch - In [tractate] Bava Kamma (50b), [the Gemara] explains what is a cistern and what is a ditch.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:9:2.english: That is within it - That is in the field.

Rashi on Eruvin 55b:9:3.hebrew: בית שבספינה - לא קביע ליה דוכתא — פעמים שהוא בתוך שבעים לעיר, פעמים שאינו:
Rashi on Eruvin 55b:9:3.english: A house on a boat - It does not have a fixed location; sometimes it is within seventy [cubits] of the city, [and] sometimes it is not.

Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:13:1.hebrew: לא צריכא להשלים - פי' בקונטרס: שהבנין לא הוי ד' אמות על ד' אמות, והמערה משלימה לד' אמות. ונראה לר"י דצריך שיהא בנין רוב ד' אמות. ועוד יש לפרש "להשלים": דיש בבנין ד' אמות, וקאמר שמשלימה למערה לצרפה לבנין, ואין מתחילין למדוד אלא מסוף המערה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:13:1.english: "No, it is necessary [only] to complete" - Rashi explained that the structure is not four cubits by four cubits, and the cave completes it to four cubits. And it appears to the Ri that the structure must be the majority of the four cubits. And furthermore, one can explain "to complete" [as meaning] that there are [already] four cubits in the structure, and [the Gemara] is saying that it completes the cave to join it to the structure, and they do not begin to measure except from the end of the cave.

Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:23:1.hebrew: כל עיר שאין בה ירק - פי': לפי שניקח בזול, ויכול לעסוק בתורה. והא דאמר בפ' תולין (שבת דף קמ:): "בר בי רב לא ליכול ירקא משום דגריר", משמע שגורם לו להוציא הרבה באכילת לחם — התם מיירי בירק חי, אבל מבושל — טוב, ומשביע בדבר קל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:23:1.english: Any city that does not have vegetables - Explanation: Because it is purchased cheaply, and [thus] he is able to engage in Torah [study]. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Tolin (Shabbat 140b): "A student of a Torah academy should not eat vegetables because it stimulates [the appetite]," which implies that it causes him to spend a lot on eating bread — there it is dealing with raw vegetables, but cooked [vegetables are] good, and sate [a person] with something inexpensive.

Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:8:1.hebrew: נפש שיש בו ד' אמות - גבי נפש הזכיר ד' אמות ולא דירה — משום דסתמיה עשוי לדירה, כדפ"ה. וגבי גשר וקבר הזכיר דירה. ומה שלא הזכיר ד' אמות — לאו משום דסתמייהו ד' אמות, דהא קבר סתמא לא הוי ד' אמות; אלא כיון שהזכיר בית דירה, כאילו הזכיר ד' אמות, דפחות מד' אמות לא הוי דירה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 55b:8:1.english: "A monument [nefesh] that has four cubits" - Regarding a monument [nefesh], [the baraita] mentioned four cubits and not a dwelling [space], because it is ordinarily made for dwelling, as explained by the Kunteres [Rashi]. And regarding a bridge and a grave, it mentioned a dwelling [space]; and that which it did not mention four cubits is not because they are ordinarily four cubits, for an ordinary grave is not four cubits. Rather, once it mentioned a dwelling space, it is as if it mentioned four cubits, for [an area of] less than four cubits does not constitute a dwelling.
